newsitem.title: UK: Oil continues weak, near four month low.
newsitem.headline: Oil continues weak, near four month low.

text.p: Oil rebounded from testing four month lows on Monday but traders and analysts say that the market remains vulnerable.

London March futures for the bellwether Brent crude blend slid as low as $22.00 per barrel, a level last seen on September 23, but recovered to trade at $22.11 by 1700 GMT, down from Friday's close of $22.26.
"It is just holding its own and does not look as if it is reviving. I would not be surprised to see it dip below $22.00," said Tony Machuchak, a trader at Credit Lyonannais Rouse in London.
Traders said there was little fundamental reason for oil's week-long losing streak.
"A lot of funds had been on the long side of the market and they have turned sellers. The trade is mixed," said Machuchak.
Traders said that last week's figures from the American Petroleum Institute which showed a drop larger-than-expected drop in crude oil inventories should have been supportive.
"Unless we get some kind of fundamental pickup, this market looks as though is bound lower," said Charles Gray, an analyst at Prudential Bache International.
This week's API figures, due late evening London time on Tuesday, are expected to be less supportive for energy markets, especially heating oil.

"At Thanksgiving in November we were 19 million barrels below the year ago level for distillate inventories, at last count we 300,000 below, so it is not surprising the market has slipped down," said Gray.

Figures from the API last week showed that distillate stocks, which include heating oil and low sulphur diesel, fell by 2.95 million barrels to 122.5 million barrels, or just 330,000 barrels less than the same period a year earlier.
"The perception is that we are running an inventory pattern similar to last year and we do not have a weather pattern similar to last year so there is pressure on prices," he said.

After a harsh winter last year, U.S. weather patterns on the east coast in 1997 have been relatively benign, although there are signs that a cold airstream is set to take hold for the next six to 10 days.
European heating oil fell through the $200 per tonne level and was trading around $197.50 by 1600 GMT.
"Weather and inventories are the keys for the next couple of days," said Prudential Bache's Gray.
